headline: Committee discusses County purchase of two West Maui water systems for up to $6 million

meeting.body: Maui County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee
meeting.summary: The committee discussed buying two private water systems priced at $3.5 million and $2.5 million; the chair said the item was for discussion only. It is expected at Council Member Sugimura's committee on August 4, and the County will not buy without PUC approval.
meeting.recap: The total price is up to $6 million, not counting closing costs.[[0:05:01]] The larger system has three wells, two tanks and 402 active connections.[[0:09:11]] Its price is $3.5 million, and it was appraised at $8,056,000.[[0:09:29]] The smaller system's price is $2.5 million, and it was appraised at $1.987 million.[[0:14:15]] The water department said the sellers would run the systems for about six months during the handover.[[0:27:15]] A testifier said 77% of West Maui water systems are owned by private entities.[[0:43:16]] Another testifier supported the purchase but questioned paying above the appraised value for one system.[[0:45:00]] The County would buy the companies' assets, not the companies themselves.[[0:56:12]] The department said the County will not buy the systems if the PUC does not approve the sale.[[1:01:39]] An official said only PUC approval is needed for the purchase itself.[[1:47:39]] The chair said the item was for discussion only.[[2:04:10]] The item is expected at Council Member Sugimura's committee on August 4.[[2:04:23]] If the council acts in August, closing could come around April next year.[[2:05:04]]
meeting.next: The administration plans to answer follow-up questions from committee staff, ideally by the August 4 meeting. After committee approval, the item would go to the full council for final approval. Once the council approves, the County would start the PUC process. Staff were asked to note a request to clarify when approval from a state water agency is needed.

moments.q: Question on purchase price versus appraised value
